Maps and finding your way back

Two maps show the generated terrain. You can mark places, set a destination and search for biomes. Your own builds are not drawn on the maps, so save a place before you travel far.

Voxelgame main dd29d91 · 5 min read · Everyone · feature ledger · all guides

Two maps

The compact map is a small north-up view in the top-right corner. It shows about 128 m around you and is on by default. The fullscreen map covers 512 m at first and can zoom out to about 131 km. Compact map Fullscreen world map

Key or actionWhat it does
MShow or hide the compact map.
Shift + MOpen or close the fullscreen map.
EscClose the fullscreen map.
Good to know. The maps show generated terrain only. Blocks you place or dig do not appear on them.

Look around the fullscreen map

  1. Press Shift + M to open the map. When you play offline, the world pauses while it is open. On a server, the world keeps running.
  2. Scroll the mouse wheel over the map to zoom in or out.
  3. Drag with the left mouse button to look around. Dragging does not move you.
  4. Press BACK TO PLAYER in the side panel to centre the map on you again.

The readout under the map shows the X and Z position under the cursor and its distance from you. With the cursor off the map, it shows the map centre. Player arrow on the map Your position is a gold arrow that points the way you face.

Mark places

  1. Open the fullscreen map.
  2. Right-click the spot you want. The game adds a pin named Marker 1, Marker 2 and so on, and sets it as your destination.
  3. Right-click an existing pin to remove it.

Markers use the same 16-place limit as the Journal. Rename them in the Journal to give them a clear name. Right-click map markers

Careful. Right-clicking a pin removes it even when it is a named Journal place. If the game says the Journal is full, remove a place first.

Save places in the Journal

  1. Press E, then Tab to reach the Journal. You can also click the Journal button on the fullscreen map.
  2. Type a name and an optional note in the Name and Note fields. Press Enter to finish typing.
  3. Click Pin this location to save the spot where you stand. A blank name becomes Place 1, Place 2 and so on.
  4. Click a place to select it, make it your destination, or change its text. Click Save selected note to keep the changes.

The Journal holds 16 places and lists each one with its distance from you. Use Prev and Next to page through them. Places are saved per world. Journal places and notes

Set a destination

The destination is the place the maps and the screen point to. It can be a map marker, a Journal place or an expedition site. Destinations: map marker, light beacon and on-screen marker

  • On both maps it shows as an amber +.
  • In the world it shows as an amber light column about 320 m tall.
  • On screen it shows as a gold diamond with the name and distance. The diamond sticks to the screen edge when the place is out of view. It reads HERE within 3 m.

There is no clear button. Pick another place to change the destination, or remove the selected place to clear it, but only when that place is the destination. Removing another place keeps the destination. With no destination, the maps show your home crate as a + instead. Home crate: establish, storage, repair, pack up

Find a biome or landmark

  1. Open the fullscreen map and click the search field on the left.
  2. Type a name, such as crystal, meteorite, caldera or lava tunnel. The list filters as you type.
  3. Press Enter, or click a result. The map centres on the first match, highlights it in cyan and drops a pin with the distance and coordinates.
  4. Press FIND NEXT to search outward for another match, or CLEAR to remove the pin and highlight.

The locator does not move you. Pan the map first if you want to search from another spot, because the search starts at the map centre. Map locator: find biomes and landmarks The list includes Volcano, Cliff island, Mountain range and all 92 biomes.

Travel by map (creative only)

In creative you can jump to a place from the map. Survival maps are a chart only.

  1. Click a spot on the fullscreen map without dragging. You land on a clear spot there.
  2. Or click the COORDINATES field, type X Z, or X Y Z for an exact height, and press Enter or TELEPORT.
Careful. Teleporting does not save where you came from, and there is no go back button. Save a Journal place before you jump. You must leave a vehicle or boat helm first. Click the map to travel (creative) Teleport by coordinates (creative)

In survival, clicking the map only shows a reminder. Zooming, dragging, the locator and markers still work. The map in survival (chart only, no fog of war)

Read your coordinates

The small readout at the top right shows FPS, your X, Y and Z in metres, and your biome. It is on by default. Turn it off in Settings > Debug with FPS and coordinates. It is hidden while a panel is open. Coordinates and biome readout

  • North is -Z and east is +X.
  • Write the numbers down before a long trip. They are the same numbers the coordinates field uses.

Get back to a lost build

  1. Stand at the build and open the Journal. Type a name in the Name box, then press Pin this location. To rename a place, select it, edit the name and press Save selected note.
  2. Before you travel far, open the fullscreen map and check the place shows as a pin.
  3. To return, select the place in the Journal and make it your destination. Then follow the beacon or the diamond.

The maps show terrain, not your builds. A destination pin is the way back when a build is hard to recognise in the terrain.
